translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Ma Qi reported: Mengyang and the Bian dikes were patched—the river could not take Bian city.

sentences.zh: 自今河勢趨北，來歲春首擬于中道疏決，以解南北兩岸之危。

translations.literal: From now river force trends north; next year spring head plans mid-course dredge and breach, to relieve south and north both banks' peril.
translations.idiomatic: The current was running north; next spring he would cut the mid-channel to ease both banks.

sentences.zh: 凡計工八百七十余萬 ，可於正月終興工。

translations.literal: All reckoned labor eight hundred seventy-odd ten-thousands, can at first month end raise work.
translations.idiomatic: The job totaled 8.7 million-odd work units, to start at month's end.

sentences.zh: 臣乞前期再往河上監視。

translations.literal: Your subject begs to go beforehand again to the river to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to return early to the river.

sentences.zh: 」上以所言付尚書省，而治檢覆河堤並守漲官等罪有差。

translations.literal: The emperor because the words given to Secretariat, and punished inspecting river dikes and flood-watch officials' crimes by degree.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the Secretariat; inspectors and flood-watch officers were punished by degree.

sentences.zh: 他日，尚書省奏事，上語及河防事，馬琪奏言：「臣非敢不盡心，然恐智力有所不及。

translations.literal: Another day, Secretariat memorialized affairs; the emperor spoke of river-defense affairs; Ma Qi memorialized: "Your subject does not dare not exhaust heart, yet fear intelligence and strength have what cannot reach.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ma Qi told the emperor he had done his utmost but might lack wit—

sentences.zh: 若別差官相度，儻有奇畫，亦未可知。

translations.literal: If separately dispatch officials to survey, perhaps there is strange plan—also not yet known.
translations.idiomatic: another survey might find a better plan—

sentences.zh: 如適與臣策同，方來興功，亦庶幾稍寬朝延憂顧。

translations.literal: If it happens to match your subject's policy, then come raise work—also perhaps slightly widen court worry and care."
translations.idiomatic: and if it matched his, work could proceed with less court anxiety."

sentences.zh: 」上然之，命翰林待制奧屯忠孝權尚書戶部侍郎、太府少監溫昉權尚書工部侍郎，行戶、工部事，修治河防，且諭之曰：「汝二人皆朕所素識，以故委任，冀副朕意。

translations.literal: The emperor approved, ordered Hanlin awaiting edict Aotun Zhongxiao acting Revenue director, Palace Storehouse vice director Wen Fang acting Works director, traveling Works affairs, repair river defense; and instructed them: "You two are both Our long-known—therefore entrusted, hope to fulfill Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed and sent Aotun Zhongxiao (acting Revenue) and Wen Fang (acting Works) to the river. "You are men I know—do not fail me.

sentences.zh: 如有錯失，亦不汝容。」

translations.literal: If there is error and loss, also not spare you."
translations.idiomatic: Err and I will not spare you."

sentences.zh: 承安元年七月，敕自今沿河傍側州、府、縣官雖部除者皆勿令員闕。

translations.literal: Cheng'an 1 seventh month, edict from now along-river neighboring prefectures and counties' officials though centrally posted—all do not let posts vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng'an 1, seventh month: along-river posts would not be left vacant even for central appointees.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年九月，敕御史台官：「河防利害初不與卿等事，然台官無所不問，應體究者亦體究之。

translations.literal: Taihe 2 ninth month, edict Censorate officials: "River-defense harm and benefit at first not with you and others' affair—yet Censorate officials have nothing not asked; what should be inspected, also inspect."
translations.idiomatic: Taihe 2, ninth month: the Censorate was told river defense was their business too—inspect what ought to be inspected.

sentences.zh: 」五年二月，以崔守真言：「黃河危急，芻槁物料雖雲折稅，每年不下五六次，或名為和買，而未嘗還其直。

translations.literal: Year 5 second month, because Cui Shouzhen said: "Yellow River urgent and perilous; forage and material though said commuted tax, each year not below five or six times, or named negotiated purchase, yet never returned its price."
translations.idiomatic: Year 5: Cui Shouzhen reported that though fodder was commuted or "negotiated purchase," payment came five or six times a year and was never made.

sentences.zh: 」敕委右三部司正郭澥、御史中丞孟鑄講究以聞。

translations.literal: Edict entrusted Right Three Departments director Guo Xie and Censor-in-chief Meng Zhu to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xie and Censor-in-chief Meng Zhu were ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 澥等言：「大名府、鄭州等處自承安二年以來，所科芻槁未給價者，計錢二十一萬九千餘貫。

translations.literal: Xie and others said: "Daming Prefecture, Zhengzhou and other places from Cheng'an 2 since, forage levied without price given, reckoned cash two hundred ten thousand nine thousand-odd strings."
translations.idiomatic: They found 219,000-odd strings unpaid for fodder from Daming, Zhengzhou, and elsewhere since Cheng'an 2.

sentences.zh: 」遂命以各處見錢差能幹官同各州縣清強官一一酬之，續令按察司體究。

translations.literal: Then ordered each place's cash on hand, dispatch capable officials with each prefecture and county strong officials one by one to repay; further ordered inspection office to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Capable officers were to repay county by county from local cash; the inspection office would follow up.

sentences.zh: 宣宗貞祐三年十一月壬申，上遣參知政事侯摯祭河神於宜村。

translations.literal: Xuanzong Zhenyou 3 eleventh month renshen, the emperor sent participation councillor Hou Zhi to sacrifice to the river god at Yicun.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong, Zhenyou 3, eleventh month, renshen day: Hou Zhi sacrificed to the river god at Yicun.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，單州刺史顏盞天澤言：「守禦之道，當決大河使北流德、博、觀、滄之境。

translations.literal: Year 3 fourth month, Danzhou prefect Yan Zhan Tianze said: "Defense path should breach great river to make north flow through De, Bo, Guan, Cang territory.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, year 3: Danzhou prefect Yan Zhan Tianze said defense meant breaching the great river north through De, Bo, Guan, and Cang.

sentences.zh: 今其故堤宛然猶在，工役不勞，水就下必無漂沒之患。

translations.literal: Now its old dike still exists as before, labor not toilsome, water going down surely without drift-drown calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The old dike still stood—the work was light, and the current running downhill would not drown the land.

sentences.zh: 而難者若不以犯滄鹽場損國利為說，必以浸沒河北良田為解。

translations.literal: But those who object, if they do not argue that encroaching on the Cang salt works harms state revenue, invariably cite inundation of Hebei fertile fields as their reason.
translations.idiomatic: Objectors who skip the argument about damaging the Cang salt works always fall back on flooding Hebei's good farmland.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗聞河側故老言，水勢散漫，則淺不可以馬涉，深不可以舟濟，此守禦之大計也。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard elders by the river say that when the water spreads wide it is too shallow for horses to ford and too deep for boats to cross—this is the great plan for defense.
translations.idiomatic: River elders say dispersed water is too shallow for horses and too deep for boats—a cornerstone of defense.

sentences.zh: 若日浸民田，則河徙之後，淤為沃壤，正宜耕墾，收倍于常，利孰大焉。

translations.literal: If it daily inundates the people's fields, then after the river shifts the silt becomes fertile soil, just right for plowing—harvests double the norm; what profit is greater?
translations.idiomatic: Daily flooding sounds dire, but after the river moves the silt turns to rich soil and yields can double—what gain compares?

sentences.zh: 若失此計，則河南一路兵食不足，而河北、山東之民皆瓦解矣！

translations.literal: If this plan is lost, then Henan Route will lack army grain, and the people of Hebei and Shandong will all collapse!
translations.idiomatic: Lose this plan and Henan Route runs short of army grain while Hebei and Shandong unravel.

sentences.zh: 」詔命議之。

translations.literal: 」An edict ordered deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the matter debated.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，延州刺史溫撒可喜言：「近世河離故道，自衛東南而流，由徐、邳入海，以此，河南之地為狹。

translations.literal: Fourth year, third month: Yanzhou inspector Wen Saxike said: "In recent times the river left its old course, flowing southeast from Weizhou and entering the sea through Xu and Pi—thereby the lands of Henan have grown narrow.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year Yanzhou inspector Wen Saxike said: "Lately the river has left its old channel, running southeast from Weizhou to the sea via Xu and Pi, which has pinched Henan's territory.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見新鄉縣西河水可決使東北，其南有舊堤，水不能溢，行五十餘裏與清河合，則由浚州、大名、觀州、清州、柳口入海，此河之故道也，皆有舊堤，補其缺罅足矣！

translations.literal: Your subject observes that west of Xinxiang County the river could be breached to run northeast; south of it old dikes would hold back overflow; going fifty-odd li it would join the Qing River, then through Junzhou, Daming, Guanzhou, Qingzhou, and Liukou enter the sea—this is the river's old course, all with old dikes; patching gaps and cracks suffices!
translations.idiomatic: West of Xinxiang the water could be cut northeast; old dikes to the south would contain it; after fifty-odd li it would meet the Qing River and reach the sea via Junzhou, Daming, Guanzhou, Qingzhou, and Liukou—the old course, already diked, needing only gaps filled.

sentences.zh: 如此則山東、大名等路，皆在河南，而河北諸郡亦得其半，退足以為禦備之計，進足以壯恢復之基。

translations.literal: Thus Shandong, Daming, and other routes would all lie south of the river, while Hebei commanderies would also regain half; in retreat enough for defense, in advance enough to strengthen recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong and Daming would lie south of the river, Hebei would recover half its ground—enough for defense in retreat and a stronger base for recovery.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「南岸居民，既已籍其河夫修築河堰，營作戍屋，又使轉輸芻糧，賦役繁殷，倍於他所，夏秋租稅，猶所未論，乞減其稍緩者，以寬民力。

translations.literal: 」He also said: "South-bank residents, already registered as river corvée to build dikes and guard houses, are also made to haul fodder—levies heavier than elsewhere, summer and autumn land tax not yet counted; beg to reduce the lighter items to ease the people.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked relief for south-bank residents already drafted for dikes and guard posts and for fodder transport—burdens heavier than elsewhere, land tax aside—to trim the lighter levies.

sentences.zh: 」事下尚書省，宰臣謂：「河流東南舊矣。

translations.literal: 」The matter went to the Secretariat; the chief ministers said: "The river's southeast course is long established.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat received it; the chief ministers said the southeast course was entrenched.

sentences.zh: 一旦決之，恐故道不容，衍溢而出，分為數河，不復可收。

translations.literal: To breach it in a day fears the old channel cannot hold it, spill out, split into several rivers, and never be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden breach might overflow the old channel, split into many streams, and prove irreversible.

sentences.zh: 水分則淺狹易渡，天寒輒凍，禦備愈難，此甚不可！

translations.literal: Divided water runs shallow and narrow, easy to cross; when heaven turns cold it freezes—defense grows harder; this must not be done!
translations.idiomatic: Split channels run shallow and freeze in winter, easing enemy crossings—this must not be done.

sentences.zh: 」詔但令量宜減南岸郡縣居民之賦役。

translations.literal: 」An edict only ordered appropriate reduction of levies on south-bank prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: The edict only ordered easing levies on south-bank prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 五年夏四月，敕樞密院，沿河要害之地，可壘石岸，仍置撒星樁、陷馬塹以備敵。

translations.literal: Fifth year, summer, fourth month: an order to the Privy Council that along the river at strategic points stone banks could be piled, with scattered-star piles and horse-trap moats set to guard against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, year five, the Privy Council was told to build stone banks along the river at key points and add scattered-star piles and horse-trap moats against attack.

sentences.zh: 金都于燕，東去潞水五十里，故為閘以節高良河、白蓮潭諸水，以通山東、河北之粟。

translations.literal: The Jin capital was at Yan; fifty li east lay the Lu River—so sluices were made to regulate the Gaoliang River, Bailian Pond, and other waters to move grain from Shandong and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: With the capital at Yan, fifty li east stood the Lu River; sluices regulated the Gaoliang River, Bailian Pond, and other waters to feed Shandong and Hebei grain inland.

sentences.zh: 凡諸路瀕河之城，則置倉以貯傍郡之稅，若恩州之臨清、曆亭，景州之將陵、東光，清州之興濟、會川，獻州及深州之武強，是六州諸縣皆置倉之地也。

translations.literal: Every route city on the river set granaries for neighboring commandery tax: Enzhou's Linqing and Liting, Jingzhou's Jiangling and Dongguang, Qingzhou's Xingji and Huichuan, Xianzhou and Shenzhou's Wuqiang—these six prefectures' counties were all granary sites.
translations.idiomatic: River cities stored tax grain from nearby commanderies—Linqing and Liting in Enzhou, Jiangling and Dongguang in Jingzhou, Xingji and Huichuan in Qingzhou, Wuqiang in Xian and Shen—the six prefectures' granary counties.

sentences.zh: 其通漕之水，舊黃河行滑州、大名、恩州、景州、滄州、會州之境，漳水東北為禦河，則通蘇門、獲嘉、新鄉、衛州、浚州、黎陽、衛縣、彰德、磁州、洺州之饋，衡水則經深州會於滹沱，以來獻州、清州之餉，皆合于信安海壖。

translations.literal: The grain-transport waters: the old Yellow River ran through Huazhou, Daming, Enzhou, Jingzhou, Cangzhou, and Huizhou; the Zhang River turned northeast as the Yu River, feeding Sumen, Huojia, Xinxiang, Weizhou, Junzhou, Liyang, Weixian, Zhangde, Cizhou, and Mingzhou; the Heng River joined the Hutuo at Shenzhou for Xian and Qing supplies—all converging at the Xin'an coastal stores.
translations.idiomatic: Grain routes: the old Yellow River through Huazhou, Daming, Enzhou, Jingzhou, Cangzhou, and Huizhou; the Zhang as the northeast Yu River to Sumen, Huojia, Xinxiang, Weizhou, Junzhou, Liyang, Weixian, Zhangde, Cizhou, and Mingzhou; the Heng meeting the Hutuo at Shenzhou for Xian and Qing—all ending at Xin'an coastal depots.

sentences.zh: 溯流而至通州，由通州入閘，十餘日而後至於京師。

translations.literal: Going upstream to Tongzhou, through Tongzhou's sluice, more than ten days then to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Upstream to Tongzhou, through its sluice, then ten-odd days to the capital.

sentences.zh: 其他若霸州之巨馬河，雄州之沙河，山東之北清河，皆其灌輸之路也。

translations.literal: Elsewhere Buzhou's Juma River, Xiongzhou's Sha River, and Shandong's North Qing River were all feeder routes.
translations.idiomatic: Buzhou's Juma, Xiongzhou's Sha, and Shandong's North Qing River also fed the network.

sentences.zh: 然自通州而上，地峻而水不留，其勢易淺，舟膠不行，故常徙事陸挽，人頗艱之。

translations.literal: Yet above Tongzhou the ground rose and water did not linger; the current easily shoaled, boats stuck and could not go—so they constantly shifted to land haulage, to people's great hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Above Tongzhou the land rose, water did not hold, channels shoaled, and boats grounded—so haulage went by land at great cost.

sentences.zh: 世宗之世，言者請開盧溝金口以通漕運，役眾數年，竟無成功，事見《盧溝河》。

translations.literal: In Shizong's reign memorialists asked to open the Lugou golden mouth for grain transport; corvée ran years and in the end failed—see "Lugou River."
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong, memorialists urged opening the Lugou golden mouth for transport; years of labor failed—see "Lugou River."

sentences.zh: 其後亦以閘河或通或塞，而但以車挽矣。

translations.literal: Later the sluice river sometimes open, sometimes blocked, and they relied only on cart haulage.
translations.idiomatic: Later the sluice river ran intermittently and carts alone carried the grain.

sentences.zh: 其制，春運以冰消行，暑雨畢。

translations.literal: The rule: spring transport ran from ice-out until summer rains ended.
translations.idiomatic: Spring convoys ran from ice-out until the summer rains ended.

sentences.zh: 秋運以八月行，冰凝畢。

translations.literal: Autumn transport ran from the eighth month until ice set.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn convoys ran from the eighth month until freeze-up.

sentences.zh: 其綱將發也。

translations.literal: When the convoy was to depart—
translations.idiomatic: When a convoy was to sail—

sentences.zh: 乃合眾，以所載之粟苴而封之，先以付所卸之地，視與所封樣同則受。

translations.literal: they assembled the crowd, wrapped the loaded grain in straw and sealed it, first delivered to the unloading place, and accepted only if it matched the sealed sample.
translations.idiomatic: crews bundled and sealed the grain, sent samples ahead to the discharge point, and accepted cargo only if it matched the seal.

sentences.zh: 凡綱船以前期三日修治，日裝一綱，裝畢以三日啟行。

translations.literal: Every convoy ship was repaired three days before; one convoy loaded per day; when loading finished, three days then departure.
translations.idiomatic: Ships were overhauled three days ahead; one convoy loaded per day; three days after loading, they sailed.

sentences.zh: 計道裏分溯流、沿流為限，至所受之倉，以三日卸，又三日給收付。

translations.literal: Distance was reckoned by li, limits set for upstream and downstream; at the receiving granary three days to unload, three more to issue receipts.
translations.idiomatic: Mileage set upstream and downstream limits; three days to unload at the granary and three to issue receipts.

sentences.zh: 凡挽漕腳直，水運鹽每石百里四十八文，米五十文一分二厘七毫，粟四十文一分三毫，錢則每貫一文七分二厘八毫。

translations.literal: Porterage for grain haul: salt by water 48 wen per shi per 100 li; rice 50 wen 1 fen 2 li 7 hao; millet 40 wen 1 fen 3 hao; cash 1 wen 7 fen 2 li 8 hao per string.
translations.idiomatic: Water porterage: salt 48 wen per shi per 100 li; rice 50.127 wen; millet 40.13 wen; cash 1.728 wen per string.

sentences.zh: 陸運傭直，米每石百里百一十二文一分五毫，粟五十七文六分八厘四毫，錢每貫三文九厘六毫。

translations.literal: Land porterage: rice 112 wen 1 fen 5 hao per shi per 100 li; millet 57 wen 6 fen 8 li 4 hao; cash 3 wen 9 li 6 hao per string.
translations.idiomatic: Land porterage: rice 112.15 wen per shi per 100 li; millet 57.684 wen; cash 3.96 wen per string.

sentences.zh: 餘物每百斤行百里，平路則春冬百三十一文五分，夏秋百五十七文八分，山路則春冬百四十九文，夏秋二百一文。

translations.literal: Other goods per 100 jin per 100 li on level roads: spring and winter 131 wen 5 fen; summer and autumn 157 wen 8 fen; mountain roads spring and winter 149 wen, summer and autumn 201 wen.
translations.idiomatic: Other goods per 100 jin per 100 li: level roads 131.5 wen spring/winter, 157.8 wen summer/autumn; mountain roads 149 wen spring/winter, 201 wen summer/autumn.

sentences.zh: 凡使司院務納課傭直，春冬九十文三分，夏秋百一十四文。

translations.literal: Porterage for yamen and office tax delivery: spring and winter 90 wen 3 fen; summer and autumn 114 wen.
translations.idiomatic: Office tax porterage: 90.3 wen spring/winter, 114 wen summer/autumn per 100 jin per 100 li.

sentences.zh: 諸民戶射賃官船漕運者，其腳直以十分為率，初年克二分，二年克一分八厘，三年克一分七厘，四年克一分五厘，五年以上克一分。

translations.literal: Households who bid to rent official ships for transport: porterage on a ten-part scale—first year 2 parts withheld, second year 1.8 fen, third 1.7 fen, fourth 1.5 fen, fifth year and after 1 fen.
translations.idiomatic: Households renting official transport ships paid porterage on a ten-part scale: 20% the first year, then 18%, 17%, 15%, and 10% from the fifth year on.

sentences.zh: 初，世宗大定四年八月，以山東大熟，詔移其粟以實京師。

translations.literal: At first, Shizong Dading 4, eighth month: because Shandong had a great harvest, an edict moved its grain to fill the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Dading 4 Shizong, with Shandong in great harvest, ordered grain moved to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十月，上出近郊，見運河湮塞，召問其故。

translations.literal: Tenth month: the emperor went to the suburbs and saw the transport canal silted; he asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the emperor rode out, saw the canal choked, and asked why.

sentences.zh: 主者雲戶部不為經畫所致。

translations.literal: The responsible official said the Revenue Bureau had not planned it.
translations.idiomatic: Officials blamed the Revenue Bureau for lack of planning.

sentences.zh: 上召戶部侍郎曹望之，責曰：「有河不加浚，使百姓陸運勞甚，罪在汝等。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Revenue Vice Minister Cao Wangzhi and reproved him: "You have a river yet do not dredge it, making the people haul by land with great toil—the fault lies with you.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Revenue Vice Minister Cao Wangzhi: "You leave a river undredged and force the people into costly land haulage—the fault is yours.

sentences.zh: 朕不欲即加罪，宜悉力使漕渠通也。

translations.literal: I do not wish to punish you at once; you must use all your strength to make the transport canal passable."
translations.idiomatic: I will not punish you yet—exert every effort to open the transport canal."

sentences.zh: 」五年正月，尚書省奏，可調夫數萬，上曰：「方春不可勞民，令宮籍監戶、東宮親王人從、及五百內裏軍夫浚治。

translations.literal: 」Fifth year, first month: the Secretariat memorialized that tens of thousands of laborers could be mobilized; the emperor said: "It is spring—do not weary the people; order palace registry households, Eastern Palace princes' followers, and five hundred inner-palace troops to dredge."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year five the Secretariat proposed tens of thousands of laborers; the emperor said spring must not burden the people and ordered palace registry households, Eastern Palace followers, and five hundred inner-palace troops to dredge.

sentences.zh: 」二十一年，以八月京城儲積不廣，詔沿河恩獻等六州粟百萬余石運至通州，輦入京師。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year: because capital stores were not ample, an edict moved over a million shi of grain from the six river-bank prefectures En and Xian to Tongzhou, then carted into the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-one, with capital stores low, over a million shi from En, Xian, and four other river prefectures went to Tongzhou and then by cart to the capital.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年四月，尚書省奏：「遼東、北京路米粟素饒，宜航海以達山東。

translations.literal: Mingchang 3, fourth month: the Secretariat memorialized: "Liaodong and Beijing Route grain has always been abundant; sea transport should reach Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Mingchang 3 the Secretariat said Liaodong and Beijing routes were rich in grain and should feed Shandong by sea.

sentences.zh: 昨以按視東京近海之地，自大務清口並咸平銅善館皆可置倉貯粟以通漕運，若山東、河北荒歉，即可運以相濟。

translations.literal: Recently, inspecting seas near Dongjing, from Dawu Qingkou through Xianping Tongshan guan granaries could be placed to open transport; if Shandong and Hebei suffered dearth, grain could be shifted to aid them."
translations.idiomatic: A recent survey from Dawu Qingkou to Xianping found sites for coastal granaries; if Shandong or Hebei failed, grain could be shifted to help."

sentences.zh: 」制可。

translations.literal: 」Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 承安五年，邊河倉州縣，可令折納菽二十萬石，漕以入京，驗品級養馬於俸內帶支，仍漕麥十萬石，各支本色。

translations.literal: Cheng'an 5: river-bank granary prefectures and counties could commute twenty thousand shi of beans, transport them to the capital, verify grades to maintain horses from salaries, and also transport one hundred thousand shi of wheat, each paid in kind.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 5, river granary districts could commute twenty thousand shi of beans and ten thousand shi of wheat to the capital, with grades checked for horse upkeep from salaries, all in kind.

sentences.zh: 乃命都水監丞田櫟相視運糧河道。

translations.literal: Then Director of Waterways Vice Commissioner Tian Li was ordered to inspect the grain-transport river course.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Waterways Vice Commissioner Tian Li was sent to survey the transport channel.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，尚書省以景州漕運司所管六河倉，歲稅不下六萬余石，其科州縣近者不下二百里，官吏取賄延阻，人不勝苦，雖近官監之亦然。

translations.literal: Taihe 1: the Secretariat said the Jingzhou grain-transport office's six river granaries yearly tax was no less than sixty thousand shi, but levied counties within two hundred li; officials took bribes and delayed, people could not bear it—even near officials supervising were the same.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 1 the Secretariat reported Jingzhou's six river granaries took sixty thousand shi yearly from counties up to two hundred li away while officials extorted and delayed—misery even under nearby supervisors.

sentences.zh: 遂命監察御史一員往來糾察之。

translations.literal: Then one investigating censor was ordered to travel back and forth to correct it.
translations.idiomatic: An investigating censor was appointed to tour and correct abuses.

sentences.zh: 五年，上至霸州，以故漕河淺澀，敕尚書省發山東、河北、河東、中都、北京軍夫六千，改鑿之。

translations.literal: Fifth year: the emperor reached Buzhou; because the old transport river was shallow and sluggish, he ordered the Secretariat to send six thousand laborers from Shandong, Hebei, Hedong, Zhongdu, and Beijing to cut a new channel.
translations.idiomatic: In year five, at Buzhou, finding the old canal shallow, he ordered six thousand laborers from Shandong, Hebei, Hedong, Zhongdu, and Beijing to cut a new channel.

sentences.zh: 犯屯田戶地者，官對給之。

translations.literal: Where it encroached on garrison-field households, the state compensated in kind.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison-field land was compensated by the state in kind.

sentences.zh: 民田則多酬其價。

translations.literal: Civilian fields were mostly paid their price.
translations.idiomatic: Civilian fields were mostly bought out at price.

sentences.zh: 六年，尚書省以凡漕河所經之地，州縣官以為無與於己，多致淺滯，使綱戶以盤淺剝載為名，奸弊百出。

translations.literal: Sixth year: the Secretariat said that wherever the transport river passed, prefectural officials treated it as none of their business and often let it shoal, letting convoy households use "shallow stripping and lightening" as a name for countless fraud.
translations.idiomatic: In year six the Secretariat complained that river prefects ignored transport channels until they shoaled, letting convoy crews fake "shallow-water stripping" for endless fraud.

sentences.zh: 於是遂定制，凡漕河所經之地，州府官銜內皆帶「提控漕河事」，縣官則帶「管勾漕河事」，俾催檢綱運，營護堤岸。

translations.literal: Then regulations were fixed: wherever the transport river passed, prefectural titles all carried "supervise grain-transport river affairs," county titles "manage grain-transport river affairs," to urge convoys and maintain dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations then required prefects to carry "supervise grain-transport river affairs" and counties "manage grain-transport river affairs" to hurry convoys and tend dikes.

sentences.zh: 為府三：大興、大名、彰德。

translations.literal: Prefectures three: Daxing, Daming, Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: Three prefectures: Daxing, Daming, Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 州十二：恩、景、滄、清、獻、深、衛、浚、滑、磁、洺、通。

translations.literal: Prefectures twelve: En, Jing, Cang, Qing, Xian, Shen, Wei, Jun, Hua, Ci, Ming, Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve prefectures: En, Jing, Cang, Qing, Xian, Shen, Wei, Jun, Hua, Ci, Ming, and Tong.

sentences.zh: 縣三十三：大名、元城、館陶、夏津、武城、曆亭、監清、吳橋、將陵、東光、南皮、清池、靖海、興濟、會川、交河、樂壽、武強、安陽、湯陰、監漳、成安、滏陽、內黃、黎陽、衛、蘇門、獲嘉、新鄉、汲、潞、武清、香河、漷陰。

translations.literal: Counties thirty-three: Daming, Yuancheng, Guantao, Xiajin, Wucheng, Liting, Jianqing, Wuqiao, Jiangling, Dongguang, Nanpi, Qingchi, Jinghai, Xingji, Huichuan, Jiaohe, Leshou, Wuqiang, Anyang, Tangyin, Jianzhang, Cheng'an, Fuyang, Neihuang, Liyang, Wei, Sumen, Huojia, Xinxiang, Ji, Lu, Wuqing, Xianghe, and Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-three counties: Daming, Yuancheng, Guantao, Xiajin, Wucheng, Liting, Jianqing, Wuqiao, Jiangling, Dongguang, Nanpi, Qingchi, Jinghai, Xingji, Huichuan, Jiaohe, Leshou, Wuqiang, Anyang, Tangyin, Jianzhang, Cheng'an, Fuyang, Neihuang, Liyang, Wei, Sumen, Huojia, Xinxiang, Ji, Lu, Wuqing, Xianghe, and Huayin.

sentences.zh: 十二月，通濟河創設巡河官一員，與天津河同為一司，通管漕河閘岸，止名天津河巡河官，隸都水監。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: the Tongji River newly set one river-patrol officer, together with the Tianjin River as one office, managing transport sluices and banks—only named Tianjin River patrol officer, subordinate to the Directorate of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month one patrol officer was added for the Tongji River, merged with Tianjin River under one office managing sluices and banks—the Tianjin River patrol officer under the Directorate of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 八年六月，通州刺史張行信言：「船自通州入閘，凡十余日方至京師，而官支五日轉腳之費。

translations.literal: Eighth year, sixth month: Tongzhou inspector Zhang Xingxin said: "Ships from Tongzhou through the sluice need more than ten days to reach the capital, yet officials pay only five days' porterage."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year eight Tongzhou inspector Zhang Xingxin said ships needed ten-odd days from Tongzhou to the capital but porterage was paid for only five.

sentences.zh: 」遂增給之。

translations.literal: 」So it was increased.
translations.idiomatic: Porterage was increased.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年，既遷於汴，以陳、潁二州瀕水，欲借民船以漕，不便。

translations.literal: Zhenyou 3: after moving the capital to Bian, because Chen and Ying bordered water and they wished to borrow civilian boats for transport—which was inconvenient—
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 3, after the move to Bian, Chen and Ying on the water made borrowing civilian boats awkward,

sentences.zh: 遂依觀州漕運司設提舉官，募船戶而籍之，命戶部勾當官往來巡督。

translations.literal: they followed Guanzhou's grain-transport office in setting a commissioner, enrolling boat households on the register, and ordering Revenue Bureau agents to patrol back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: so they copied Guanzhou's transport office with a commissioner, registered boat households, and sent Revenue agents to supervise.

sentences.zh: 四年，從右丞侯摯言，開沁水以便饋運。

translations.literal: Fourth year: following Right Vice Minister Hou Zhi's memorial, the Qin River was opened to ease supply transport.
translations.idiomatic: In year four, on Right Vice Minister Hou Zhi's advice, the Qin River was opened for supply transport.

sentences.zh: 上又念京師轉輸之勞，命出尚廄牛及官車，以助其力。

translations.literal: The emperor also minded the capital's transport toil and ordered imperial stables' oxen and official carts to help the effort.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of capital transport burdens, he also sent imperial stable oxen and official carts to help.

sentences.zh: 興定四年十月，諭皇太子曰：「中京運糧護送官，當擇其人，萬有一失，樞密官亦有罪矣！

translations.literal: Xingding 4, tenth month: he instructed the crown prince: "The Zhongjing grain escort officer must be well chosen; if there is the slightest lapse, Privy Council officials are also guilty!
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Xingding 4 he told the crown prince: "Choose the Zhongjing grain escort carefully—one slip and Privy Council officials share the guilt!

sentences.zh: 其船當用毛花輦所造兩首尾者，仍張幟如渡軍之狀，勿令敵知為糧也。

translations.literal: The boats should be the double-ended type built by the Maohua workshop, still flying banners like ferry troops—do not let the enemy know it is grain."
translations.idiomatic: Use Maohua workshop double-ended boats with ferry-style banners so enemies do not know they carry grain."

sentences.zh: 」陝西行省把胡魯言：」陝西歲運糧以助關東，民力浸困，若以舟自渭入河，順流而下，可以紓民力。

translations.literal: 」Shaanxi Branch Secretariat Ba Hulu said: "Shaanxi yearly transports grain to aid Guandong; the people's strength is worn down—if boats enter the Wei and go downriver with the current, the people's burden could be eased."
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Branch Secretariat Ba Hulu said Shaanxi's yearly grain for Guandong exhausted the people; boats from the Wei downriver could ease that burden.

sentences.zh: 」遂命嚴其偵候，如有警，則皆維于南岸。

translations.literal: 」Then he ordered strict scouting; if there was alarm, all were to moor on the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered strict scouting and, on alarm, all boats to moor on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 時朝延以邳、徐、宿、泗軍儲，京東縣挽運者歲十余萬石，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: At the time the court because Pi, Xu, Su, and Si military stores and Jingdong counties' cart transport of more than one hundred thousand shi yearly—the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The court noted Pi, Xu, Su, and Si stores and Jingdong counties' yearly carting of over one hundred thousand shi and the people's great suffering.

sentences.zh: 元光元年，遂於歸德府置通濟倉，設都監一員，以受東郡之粟。

translations.literal: Yuanguang 1: therefore at Guide Prefecture they set the Tongji granary with one director to receive eastern commandery grain.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanguang 1 Guide Prefecture gained a Tongji granary with a director to receive eastern commandery grain.

sentences.zh: 定國軍節度使李複亨言：「河南駐蹕，兵不可闕，糧不厭多，比年，少有匱乏即仰給陝西，陝西地腴歲豐，十萬石之助不難。

translations.literal: Dingguo Army jiedushi Li Fuheng said: "With the court at Henan, troops cannot be few nor grain too much; in recent years, slight shortage and Shaanxi is looked to—Shaanxi's land is fertile and years abundant; one hundred thousand shi is not hard.
translations.idiomatic: Dingguo Army jiedushi Li Fuheng said: "At Henan troops and grain must be ample; lately any shortfall turns to Shaanxi, whose fertile fields could spare one hundred thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 但以車運之費先去其半，民何以堪？

translations.literal: But cart transport's cost takes half in advance—how can the people bear it?
translations.idiomatic: Yet carting wastes half the cost upfront—how can people endure it?

sentences.zh: 宜造大船二十，由大慶關渡入河，東抵湖城，往還不過數日，篙工不過百人，使舟皆容三百五十斛，則是百人以數日運七千斛矣！

translations.literal: Large boats twenty should be built, entering the river from Daqing Pass, east to Hucheng; round trip in only days, polemen no more than one hundred; let each boat hold 350 hu—then one hundred men in days move seven thousand hu!
translations.idiomatic: Build twenty large boats from Daqing Pass into the river to Hucheng: a round trip in days, under one hundred polemen, each holding 350 hu—one hundred men could move seven thousand hu in days.

sentences.zh: 自夏抵秋可漕三千余萬斛，且無稽滯之患。

translations.literal: From summer to autumn three million-odd hu could be transported, without delay.
translations.idiomatic: From summer through autumn three million-odd hu could move without backlog.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: 」The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 時又於靈璧縣潼郡鎮設倉都監及監支納，以方開長直溝，將由萬安湖舟運入汴至泗，以貯粟也。

translations.literal: At the time they also set granary directors and receipt supervisors at Tongjun town, Lingbi County, for the Changzhi ditch being opened, intending boat transport from Wan'an Lake into Bian to Si to store grain.
translations.idiomatic: They also placed granary directors at Tongjun in Lingbi for the Changzhi ditch, planning Wan'an Lake boat transport into Bian and Si for storage.

sentences.zh: 盧溝河

translations.literal: Lugou River
translations.idiomatic: Lugou River

sentences.zh: 大定十年，議決盧溝以通京師漕運，上忻然曰：「如此，則諸路之物可徑達京師，利孰大焉！

translations.literal: Dading 10: they debated breaching the Lugou to open capital grain transport; the emperor said gladly: "If so, goods from all routes could reach the capital directly—what profit is greater!
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 10 they debated cutting the Lugou for capital transport; the emperor said gladly: "Then goods from every route could reach the capital—what gain compares?

sentences.zh: 」命計之，當役千里內民夫，上命免被災之地，以百官從人助役。

translations.literal: 」He ordered calculation; it would corvée commoners within a thousand li; the emperor ordered disaster areas exempted and officials' followers to assist labor.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered plans drawn; it would draft commoners within a thousand li, exempt disaster areas, and use officials' followers as labor.

sentences.zh: 已而，敕宰臣曰：「山東歲饑。

translations.literal: Soon after, he charged the chief ministers: "Shandong has famine this year.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he told the chief ministers: "Shandong is in famine.

sentences.zh: 工役興則妨農作，能無怨乎？

translations.literal: If works rise they hinder farming—can there be no resentment?
translations.idiomatic: Works would hinder farming—how could people not resent it?

sentences.zh: 開河本欲利民，而反取怨，不可！

translations.literal: Opening the river was meant to benefit the people, yet it draws resentment—impossible!
translations.idiomatic: The canal was meant to help the people, not breed resentment—impossible!

sentences.zh: 其姑罷之。

translations.literal: For now stop it."
translations.idiomatic: Stop it for now."

sentences.zh: 」十一年十二月，省臣奏複開之，自金口疏導至京城北入壕，而東至通州之北，入潞水，計工可八十日。

translations.literal: 」Eleventh year, twelfth month: provincial ministers memorialized to reopen it, from the golden mouth dredging to north of the capital into the moat, east to north of Tongzhou into the Lu River—estimated labor eighty days.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year eleven ministers urged reopening from the golden mouth to the capital moat and east to Tongzhou's north into the Lu River—eighty days' labor.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，上令人覆按，還奏：「止可五十日。

translations.literal: Twelfth year, third month: the emperor sent men to reinspect; they reported back: "Only fifty days needed."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year twelve reinspection reported only fifty days were needed.

sentences.zh: 」上召宰臣責曰：「所餘三十日徒妨農費工，卿等何為慮不及此。

translations.literal: 」The emperor summoned the chief ministers and reproved them: "The remaining thirty days only waste farming and labor—why did you not think of this?"
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the chief ministers: "The extra thirty days only waste farming—why did you not foresee this?"

sentences.zh: 」及渠成，以地勢高峻，水性渾濁。

translations.literal: 」When the channel was finished, the terrain was high and steep, the water muddy.
translations.idiomatic: When the channel opened, the ground was high and steep and the water muddy.

sentences.zh: 峻則奔流漩洄，齧岸善崩，濁則泥淖淤塞，積滓成淺，不能勝舟。

translations.literal: Steep ground makes rushing eddies that gnaw banks and collapse easily; muddy water silts and chokes, sediment piles shallow—boats cannot pass.
translations.idiomatic: Steep grades made swirling currents that ate the banks; mud silted the bed until boats could not pass.

sentences.zh: 其後，上謂宰臣曰：「分盧溝為漕渠，竟未見功，若果能行，南路諸貨皆至京師，而價賤矣。

translations.literal: Later the emperor told the chief ministers: "Splitting the Lugou as a transport canal has still not succeeded; if it truly could run, southern-route goods would all reach the capital and prices would fall."
translations.idiomatic: Later he told ministers: "Diverting the Lugou for transport still fails; if it worked, southern goods would flood the capital and prices would fall."

sentences.zh: 」平章政事駙馬元忠曰：「請求識河道者，按視其地。

translations.literal: 」Chief Councilor and imperial son-in-law Yuan Zhong said: "Request those who know river courses to inspect the ground."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor and imperial son-in-law Yuan Zhong asked experts to survey the ground.

sentences.zh: 」竟不能行而罷。

translations.literal: 」In the end it could not run and was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it could not operate and was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 二十五年五月，盧溝決于上陽村。

translations.literal: Twenty-fifth year, fifth month: the Lugou breached at Shangyang Village.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year twenty-five the Lugou broke at Shangyang Village.

sentences.zh: 先是，決顯通寨，詔發中都三百里內民夫塞之，至是複決，朝延恐枉費工物，遂令且勿治。

translations.literal: Earlier it had broken at Xiantong Stockade; an edict mobilized commoners within three hundred li of Zhongdu to block it; now it broke again; the court feared wasted labor and materials and ordered it not repaired for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: It had earlier broken at Xiantong Stockade and Zhongdu labor within three hundred li was drafted to seal it; when it broke again the court feared waste and ordered no repair for now.

sentences.zh: 二十七年三月，宰臣以「孟家山金口閘下視都城，高一百四十餘尺，止以射糧軍守之，恐不足恃。

translations.literal: Twenty-seventh year, third month: chief ministers said: "Below the Mengjiashan golden-mouth sluice looking toward the capital it is over 140 chi high, guarded only by archer-grain troops—hardly reliable.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year twenty-seven ministers said the Mengjiashan golden-mouth sluice stood 140-odd chi above the capital, guarded only by archer-grain troops—hardly safe.

sentences.zh: 儻遇暴漲，人或為奸，其害非細。

translations.literal: If a sudden flood comes and someone commits treachery, the harm is not small.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden flood or treachery could do great harm.

sentences.zh: 若固塞之，則所灌稻田俱為陸地，種植禾麥亦非曠土。

translations.literal: If firmly blocked, the irrigated paddies all become dry land—planting grain and wheat is not idle soil either.
translations.idiomatic: Blocking it would dry the irrigated paddies, yet grain and wheat could still be planted.

sentences.zh: 不然則更立重閘，仍於岸上置埽官廨署，及埽兵之室，庶幾可以無虞也」。

translations.literal: Otherwise set heavier sluices, still place sao offices and sao soldiers' quarters on the bank—then perhaps without worry."
translations.idiomatic: Or build heavier sluices with sao offices and barracks on the bank—then perhaps safe."

sentences.zh: 上是其言，遣使塞之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and sent envoys to block it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent envoys to seal it.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙子，詔封盧溝水神為安平侯。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, bingzi day: an edict enfeoffed the Lugou water spirit as Marquis of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day in the fourth summer month the Lugou water spirit was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anping.

sentences.zh: 二十八年五月，詔盧溝河使旅往來之津要，令建石橋。

translations.literal: Twenty-eighth year, fifth month: an edict that at Lugou River ferry crossings for envoys and travelers stone bridges should be built.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year twenty-eight an edict ordered stone bridges at Lugou ferry crossings for envoys and travelers.

sentences.zh: 未行而世宗崩。

translations.literal: Before it was carried out Shizong died.
translations.idiomatic: Before work began Shizong died.

sentences.zh: 章宗大定二十九年六月，複以涉者病河流湍急，詔命造舟，既而更命建石橋。

translations.literal: Zhangzong, Dading 29, sixth month: again because travelers suffered from the swift current, an edict ordered boats built; then again ordered stone bridges built.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Dading 29 Zhangzong again, travelers suffering from the swift current, first ordered boats, then stone bridges.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年三月成，敕命名曰廣利。

translations.literal: Mingchang 3, third month: completed; an edict named it Guangli.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Mingchang 3 it was finished and named Guangli by edict.

sentences.zh: 有司謂車駕之所經行，使客商旅之要路，請官建東西廊，令人居之。

translations.literal: The responsible offices said it was where the imperial carriage passed and merchants and travelers met; they asked the state to build east and west galleries for people to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Offices said the imperial route and merchant traffic met there and asked the state to build east and west galleries for lodgings.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「何必然，民間自應為耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Why must it be so? The people will do it themselves."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Why force it? People will build on their own."

sentences.zh: 」左丞守貞言：「但恐為豪右所占，況罔利之人多止東岸，若官築則東西兩岸俱稱，亦便於觀望也。

translations.literal: 」Left Vice Minister Shouzhen said: "But I fear powerful families will seize it; moreover profit-seekers mostly stop on the east bank—if the state builds, both banks will be equipped and convenient for oversight too."
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Minister Shouzhen said powerful families might seize the sites and profiteers clustered on the east bank—state galleries on both banks would aid oversight.

sentences.zh: 」遂從之。

translations.literal: 」So it was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 六月，盧溝堤決，詔速遏塞之，無令泛溢為害。

translations.literal: Sixth month: the Lugou dike breached; an edict to block it quickly and not let it spread harm.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Lugou dike broke; an edict ordered swift blocking lest it flood widely.

sentences.zh: 右拾遺路鐸上疏言：「當從水勢分流以行，不必補修玄同口以下、丁村以上舊堤。

translations.literal: Right Reminder Lu Duo memorialized: "Follow the water's force in diversion; there is no need to repair the old dike from below Xuantong Mouth to above Ding Village."
translations.idiomatic: Right Reminder Lu Duo urged diverting with the current rather than repairing the old dike from below Xuantong Mouth to above Ding Village.

sentences.zh: 」上命宰臣議之，遂命工部尚書胥持國及路鐸同檢視其堤道。

translations.literal: 」The emperor ordered the chief ministers to deliberate and then ordered Works Minister Xu Chiguo and Lu Duo together to inspect the dike route.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered ministers to debate and sent Works Minister Xu Chiguo with Lu Duo to inspect the dikes.

sentences.zh: 滹沱河

translations.literal: Hutuo River
translations.idiomatic: Hutuo River

sentences.zh: 大定八年六月，滹沱犯真定，命發河北西路及河間、太原、冀州民夫二萬八千，繕完其堤岸。

translations.literal: Dading 8, sixth month: the Hutuo invaded Zhending; an order mobilized twenty-eight thousand commoners from Hebei West Circuit and Hejian, Taiyuan, and Jizhou to repair its banks.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Dading 8 the Hutuo struck Zhending; twenty-eight thousand laborers from Hebei West Circuit, Hejian, Taiyuan, and Jizhou repaired its banks.

sentences.zh: 十年二月，滹沱河創設巡河官二員。

translations.literal: Tenth year, second month: two Hutuo River patrol officers were newly established.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year ten two Hutuo River patrol officers were created.

sentences.zh: 十七年，滹沱決白馬崗，有司以聞，詔遣使固塞，發真定五百里內民夫，以十八年二月一日興役，命同知真定尹鶻沙虎、同知河北西路轉運使徐偉監護。

translations.literal: Seventeenth year: the Hutuo broke at Baima Hill; the offices reported; an edict sent envoys to seal it firmly and mobilized commoners within five hundred li of Zhending; labor began second month, first day, year eighteen; ordered Associate Administrator of Zhending Gushahu and Associate Hebei West Circuit Transport Commissioner Xu Wei to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen it broke at Baima Hill; envoys were sent to seal it and Zhending drafted labor within five hundred li from the first day of the second month, year eighteen, under Associate Administrator Gushahu and Associate Transport Commissioner Xu Wei.

sentences.zh: 大定二十年春正月，詔有司修護漳河閘，所須工物一切並從官給，毋令擾民。

translations.literal: Dading 20, spring, first month: an edict ordered offices to maintain Zhang River sluices; all needed labor and materials from state supply—do not disturb the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Dading 20, offices were told to maintain Zhang River sluices with state labor and materials and not trouble the people.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年六月，漳河及盧溝堤皆決，詔命速塞之。

translations.literal: Mingchang 2, sixth month: Zhang River and Lugou dikes both breached; an edict ordered swift blocking.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Mingchang 2 the Zhang and Lugou dikes both broke; an edict ordered quick repairs.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月癸未，有司言修漳河堤埽計三十八萬餘工，詔依盧溝河例，招被水闕食人充夫，官支錢米，不足則調礙水人戶，依上支給。

translations.literal: Fourth year, spring, first month, guiwei day: the offices said repairing Zhang River dike-sao would take 380,000-odd work units; an edict followed the Lugou River precedent, recruiting flood-starved people as labor with state money and grain; if insufficient, then draft flood-affected households, paid as above.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day in the first spring month of year four offices reported 380,000-odd work units to repair Zhang River dike-sao; following the Lugou precedent, flood-starved people were hired at state pay, then flood households if needed, on the same terms.
